candidates.evidence_text: For children starting a new secondary school this year social media means they will likely always have a way of keeping in touch with friends after they leave But for past generations it was very different. Often the last day of school was the last time you saw most class mates - even if you might not realise it at the time It was something that prompted grandmother Karen Feay to track down the people she started Rivington & Blackrod Grammar School in Bolton with 60 years ago "I bumped into an old school friend and we got talking about our school memories - and it snowballed from there," she said. "We all started in 1966 which makes everyone 70 or 71 years old now." Karen and her friend Susan Hart have spent the past two years tracking down fellow school mates on social media A task she said had been more difficult for women who had changed their surnames after getting married

candidates.summary: More than 30 stores have been closed over their links to the sale of illegal vapes and cigarettes

candidates.practical_angle: Проверить, есть ли действующие ограничения, предупреждения или влияние на район сегодня.
candidates.lead: More than 30 stores have been closed over their links to the sale of illegal vapes and cigarettes
candidates.evidence_text: Inside the crackdown on illegal vapes in north-west England - BBC News Image source, Lancashire Police Image caption, Retail researchers estimate that there are about 3,600 specialist vape shops in the UK By Rachel Braund North West Published 7 minutes ago Police forces and councils across north-west England have shut vape shops and seized thousands of illegal items in the last year, new figures show. BBC analysis found more than 30 premises have been closed over their links to illegal vapes and illicit tobacco. The findings come after the Prime Minister announced plans to give councils greater powers to tackle rogue retailers and extend closure orders. Authorities say the products can pose a risk to public health and are often linked to wider criminality. Greater Manchester In Greater Manchester, police and council officers seized thousands of illegal vapes and cigarettes as part of Operation Elswick, a joint campaign targeting rogue retailers. In Manchester alone, officers removed £162,000 worth of illegal vapes from sale in the last year. Det Ch Insp Chris Woodburn, from Greater Manchester Police, said: "Our work in this area will continue as we are committed to tackling the issue of illegal vapes and cigarettes which fund wider crime and harm public health." Elsewhere, Bury Council obtained its first closure order against a shop after more than 3,000 vaping products were seized, while Rochdale recorded nine vape shop closures in the last six months. Image caption, Specialist dogs were part of the team searching premises in Operation Elswick Merseyside Liverpool City Council said it had secured 10 closure orders in the past six months, although it stressed these were linked to corner shops selling illicit tobacco rather than vaping products alone. In Wirral, Liscard Convenience Store became the 20th premises to be closed down since December 2025 after a closure order was granted by magistrates. Image source, Lancashire Police Image caption, Lancashire Police worked with officers at the council to close down two shops in Lancaster Lancashire In Lancashire, six vape shops have been closed and a further seven are currently being investigated. Lancashire Police and Trading Standards recently secured closure orders against two Lancaster city centre retailers after a series of failed inspections and test purchases. Euro Shop was found to have sold vapes to underage test purchasers as well as illicit cigarettes, while One Stop Mini Market repeatedly failed Trading Standards checks. Both were ordered to close until November. Sending a 'clear message' Supt Abbott, from Lancashire Police, said: "Securing a closure order is not a quick process. "It often takes months of dedicated work by our officers and partners to gather evidence, build a strong case and present it before the courts. "This result reflects the determination and professionalism of everyone involved in bringing these matters to a successful conclusion. "We take the concerns of our communities seriously and listen to the information provided by residents, businesses and local partners. "That information plays a vital role in helping us identify issues, gather evidence and take positive action where it is needed." Image source, PA Media Image caption, The ONS estimates that 5.4 million people aged 16+ in the UK used e-cigarettes daily Cheshire Cheshire Police has secured closure orders against 12 shops linked to illegal vape sales, including premises in Warrington, Widnes, Macclesfield, Crewe and Nantwich. Ch Supt Saf Ali said the action should send "a clear message" that illegal tobacco and vape products have no place in the county's shops. How is the government tackling it? The crackdown on vape shops announced by the government in August includes the following proposals: Changes to planning law in England which would mean every new shop selling e-cigarettes or vapes would need to apply to their local council for permission to open Tightening the definition of a vape shop in England to prevent businesses avoiding the rules by describing themselves as a general convenience store or retailer Requiring planning permission for new adult gaming centres in England, which offer 24-hour access to gambling machines New powers to extend closure orders for mini-marts and vape shops in England and Wales found to be selling illegal tobacco for up to 12 months, something previously proposed by former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer Related topics Cheshire More on this stor

candidates.lead: Ambrose Barlow was found guilty of treason and sentenced to death in 1641
candidates.evidence_text: The skull of a saint that was discovered during renovations - BBC News Image caption, The skull of St Ambrose Barlow is on display at Wardley Hall By Jen Dale North West Published 42 minutes ago On 25 April 1641, Ambrose Barlow celebrated a secret Easter Sunday mass at Morleys Hall near Astley in Greater Manchester. But, by the end of the service, the building had been surrounded by a 400-strong armed group led by a local vicar. "King Charles I issued a decree stating that all Catholic priests must leave within a month...and if they didn't, they would face the consequences of treason," said the Right Reverend John Arnold, the Bishop of Salford. King Charles I wanted to prove that he supported the Protestant faith while keeping his political enemies at bay as parliament were suspicious of his Catholic wife. The congregation urged Ambrose Barlow to hide but Arnold said he refused and instead ordered the doors to be opened and surrendered peacefully. "He didn't make any attempt to avoid arrest," said Arnold. "He was really concerned for the safety of the people attending mass - about 150 of them." Image source, Diocese of Salford Image caption, The Right Reverend John Arnold said records showed Ambrose Barlow had a "good sense of humour" and was "very mild in his character" He was taken to Lancaster Castle where he was imprisoned. After four months, he was put on trial, charged with being a priest. He was found guilty of treason and sentenced to death. "On 10 September, which is now his feast day, he was hung, drawn, and quartered," said Arnold. "And his skull was put on a pike as a demonstration to people that this is what happens if you are a Catholic." It was a warning to all who refused to conform to the state religion. Image source, Diocese of Salford Image caption, Wardley Hall has been the residence of the Bishop of Salford since 1930 The Catholic priest is the subject of a new episode of Hidden Manchester on BBC Sounds. The skull of St Ambrose Barlow is a sacred relic, which is kept at Wardley Hall in Worsley on red velvet inside a locked, glass-fronted cabinet recessed into a wall on the main staircase. Arnold said the skull was retrieved and brought to Wardley Hall, which has been the residence of the Bishop of Salford since 1930. "At that stage Wardley Hall belonged to the Downes family who were the cousins to the Barlow family," said Arnold, who resides at Wardley Hall. "Francis Downes placed the skull in a casket in the wall of the then chapel in Wardley Hall." The skull was accidentally discovered by Matthew Moreton during renovation work in 1745. The Skull of a Saint at Wardley Hall In 1641, Catholic priest Ambrose Barlow was persecuted for his beliefs. Listen on Sounds Later forensic tests in the 20th century confirmed it was the skull of Ambrose Barlow. On 25 October 1970, Pope Paul VI officially canonised 40 martyrs of England and Wales in a ceremony at St Peter's Basilica in Rome. This honoured Catholic men and women killed in the 16th and 17th centuries for their beliefs. Ambrose Barlow became Saint Ambrose Barlow. The skull of St Ambrose Barlow remains at Wardley Hall where private groups can see it by appointment. Arnold said it was unusual to have such a relic in a private collection. "It's rare for it to be in a private house, but Catholics have long had a tradition of relics, either pieces of a body of a saint or a possession of a saint," he said. "It's a way people have found of coming closer to the reality of the holiness of the person." You can listen to the Hidden Manchester series on BBC Sounds. You can also send story ideas via Whatsapp to 0808 100 2230. candidates.lead: Melissa Johns, 36, from Greater Manchester, says two weeks paternity leave is 'not enough' in 2026
candidates.evidence_text: A disabled mum from Greater Manchester has joined a campaign for better paternity leave after being "stopped in her tracks" by the challenges of adapting to motherhood alone Melissa Johns, 36, from Ashton-under-Lyne, welcomed her first child in October Despite requiring six weeks to recover from a caesarean section, Melissa - who was born without a fully formed right arm - was left to face maternity leave alone after her partner went back to work when their daughter was two weeks old She has now joined a campaign to change the law to let fathers take longer paternity leave, and to receive a bigger proportion of their salary when they do But sceptics say such changes would have a significant impact on businesses, and question how they could be afforded Melissa said: "Having one arm means that I rely on my core strength a lot more," Melissa said

candidates.lead: Non-profit initiative Found Football leaves footballs in parks to encourage children to exercise
candidates.evidence_text: Former boxing world champion Frank Bruno has distributed free footballs to local parks in support of a scheme encouraging children to get active The 64-year-old delivered 10 footballs to Southchurch Park in Southend-on-Sea and the nearby village of Hockley in Essex Ritchie Beckett, the director of non-profit initiative Found Football, is pledging to drop more of them in the county's parks before the end of the year The 44-year-old dad from Stockport said Bruno's support took the movement "to another level" and he wanted it to go "nationwide" in the future On social media, Bruno said he hoped it would prevent children from getting involved with "other activities" "If a small game of football between a few people means they won't be up to other things in the park it gets my thumbs up," said the former WBC heavyweight champion

The 36-year-old used safe houses to store the drugs before his courier Mohammed Vakas Ashraf delivered them to customer A third member of the gang, Nicola Toft helped move and hide the money, police said. But the operation came crashing down after GMP's serious organised crime group put the gang under surveillance And when police raided a safe house owned by a vulnerable male after witnessing Mohammed pay it a visit, they discovered 60kgs of cocaine and a car which had been adapted to include a secret drugs hide. A raid on a second safe house also uncovered a large stash of cash and a deta It revealed that another 70 kilograms of cocaine and heroin had been supplied by gang between April 2025 and June 2025. In total it was established that Toft was responsible for moving and concealing nearly £460,000 in drugs money

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester synagogue attack Manchester synagogue attack victim's step-daughter sent vile messages about his murder Melvin Cravitz's stepdaughter revealed she had been targeted by antisemitic trolls in the year since his murder News Damon Wilkinson Rep The step-daughter of one of the victims of the Heaton Park synagogue terror attack has told how she has received messages blaming Jews for his murder Sherelle Dresner told a memorial service at the synagogue how strangers have sent her antisemitic in the year since Melvin Cravitz's death . The 66-year-old, and Adrian Daulby, 53, were killed and three others were injured as they tried to defend the synagogue from terrorist Jiha Speaking tearfully about her experience, Ms Dresner told the 850 people gathered at Monday night's event of a 'lonely' and 'overwhelming' new world she and her family faced in the aftermath of the attack "It is hard to remember a life or world prior to Yom Kippur 2025," she said. "I have heard this new existence be described by survivors and bereaved families of other terrorist attacks as a club that no-one wants to be a part of, a club that no-one would ever choose to belong to. And Ms Dresner also described how she had received messages from strangers blaming Jews and world events for her stepfather’s murder

candidates.evidence_text: Strangeways Sources speak out on Strangeways' future in Manchester amid 'super prison' plans Strangeways could leave Manchester city centre forever View 3 Images There have long been calls to move Strangeways out of Manchester (Image: Sean Hansford | Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter and Damon Wilkinson Reporter 05:30, 06 Sep 2026 Updated 07:09, 06 Sep 2026 Plans for a new 'super prison' in the North West could help pave the way for the eventual closure of Strangeways , the Manchester Evening News understand This week Andy Burnham's government announced the contract for a new 1,700-place jail in Leyland, Lancs had been signed. It was part of a wider drive to 'ensure the country never again faces the nightmare of running out of prison spaces' But well-placed sources here in Manchester hope the move could help town hall bosses bolster their case for the potential closure of Strangeways. It comes three months after the MEN revealed that 'promising conversations' had been taking place with government about relocating the Speaking this week, Cheetham councillor Naeem Hassan welcomed the announcement of the new prison and said he hopes it helps usher in the end of Strangeways He said: "It's such a prime location in the city. I really want to see it moved. Prisons shouldn't be in city centres, it's not the right place. They should be in rural locations

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham 'Explosions' heard in Oldham as firefighters scrambled and over 100 homes without power Locals have reported hearing loud bangs before emergency services attended the scene Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 19:44, 05 Sep 2026 View Imag More than 100 homes were left without power after a fire at an electrical substation in Oldham. Locals reported hearing 'loud bangs' and 'explosions' as the fire broke out at the substation on Harewood Drive in Royton A video posted to social media showed bright orange flames lapping up inside it and smoke billowing out. The fire service were alerted with two fire engines attending the scene at around 5:10pm this evening (Saturday, September 5). Police were also said to be in attendance Firefighters used dry powder extinguishers in order to put out the blaze. No one was injured, Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) said Scores of locals on the neighbouring Thorp estate say their power cut out following the fire, with lights going out and dozens of house alarms sounding in the area simultaneously According to Electricity North West (ENW), at the time of writing, a total of 147 properties were still without power

The car was seen on its side, with a tree wedged inside the passenger side, following the collision in the early hours of this morning (September 5) The dramatic scenes unfolded at the Regent Road roundabout, in Salford just before 1am. Luckily, the driver was the only person in the vehicle They fortunately managed to escape the wreckage with 'minor injuries', according to Greater Manchester Police . Officers also arrested the driver, a man in his 20s, at the scene, but later de-arrested them Enquiries into the collision remain ongoing, GMP says. candidates.evidence_text: Crime The drugs kingpin from Oldham who claimed to have met Pablo Escobar's brother in Colombia Toseef Mohammed dealt heroin and cocaine on an 'industrial scale' View 4 Images Toseef Mohammed (Image: GMP) News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 13:07, 05 Sep 2026 A drugs kingpin from Oldham claimed to have met Pablo Escobar's brother in Colombia, police have said Toseef Mohammed is behind bars after detectives smashed a heroin and cocaine ring that supplied the class A drugs on a 'commercial scale' across the North West. The 36-year-old used safe houses to store the drugs before his courier Mohammed Vakas Ashraf delivered them to customer A third member of the gang, Nicola Toft helped move and hide the money, police said. But the operation came crashing down after GMP's serious organised crime group put the gang under surveillance And when police raided a safe house owned by a vulnerable male after witnessing Mohammed pay it a visit, they discovered 60kgs of cocaine and a car which had been adapted to include a secret drugs hide. A raid on a second safe house also uncovered a large stash of cash and a deta It revealed that another 70 kilograms of cocaine and heroin had been supplied by gang between April 2025 and June 2025. In total it was established that Toft was responsible for moving and concealing nearly £460,000 in drugs money

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre Tragedy outside Piccadilly Station as man dies after being rushed to hospital An investigation is underway News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 11:45, 05 Sep 2026 Updated 13:17, 05 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Police at the scene on L A man has tragically died after being found unresponsive near Piccadilly station . Officers were called out to London Road, near to Piccadilly Station Approach, at 6.50am this morning (September 5) Greater Manchester Police says a man in his 50s was taken to hospital after being found unresponsive, but he sadly later died. There are not currently believed to be any suspicious circumstances, but enquiries to establish the full circumstances are ongoing A large cordon was in place on London Road this morning between Aytoun Street and Store Street. Officers had erected a blue forensic tent on one part of the pavement Forensics investigators attended the scene and were seen gathering photographic evidence. The cordon has since been lifted In an initial statement, a GMP spokesperson said: "Officers were called to reports of a male unresponsive on London Road at 6:50am this morning (5 September). The male was taken to hospital where he has since sadly passed away. Enquires remain ongoing."

And he should know The Factory Records boss had first-hand experience with the pop superstar’s brusque manner after she performed at the Haçienda in 1984 for the princely sum of £50 The bargain price gig was negotiated by television executive Malcolm Gerrie, who persuaded Madonna's record company to organise her appearance at the venue as part of a one-off, live Channel 4 broadcast of cult music show The Tube View 4 Images Madonna performing at The Hacienda, Manchester, on an episode of The Tube (Image: Channel 4/The Tube/YouTube screengrab) Free ticket-holders to the Haçienda showcase on January 27, 1984 were there to see the Factory Allstars - a band pulled together for the night by members of Durutti Column, A Certain Ratio, Quando Quango and soul singer Marcel King. So they were bemused when Madonna rocked up on Flanked by two Lycra-clad backing dancers, the then 25-year-old spun and gyrated as she sang Holiday. Her brother Christopher Ciccone - who was a backing dancer at the Haçienda gig - recounted their time in Manchester in his book, Life With My Sister

Councillor Jake Austin said they were delivering what people want by increasing collections Towards the end of July, Stockport council began enforcing a long-standing rule around not collecting any bins that had the lids open. The local authority said this was to ensure the safety of bin crews based on manufacturer guidance However, council officers appeared to not tell anyone the change had taken place, even top councillors. As the public did not know about the enforcement, hundreds of bins were not collected prompting major backlash Those issues appear to have largely been resolved and last week, the council’s Liberal Democrat-administration announced major changes are coming with more collections to start later this year. From the beginning of December 2026, blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling will The council moved to four weekly collections due to financial pressures on its budget for day-to-day services in 2025. Opposition parties have overwhelmingly welcomed the move but questions remain

candidates.evidence_text: Strangeways Sources speak out on Strangeways' future in Manchester amid 'super prison' plans Strangeways could leave Manchester city centre forever View 3 Images There have long been calls to move Strangeways out of Manchester (Image: Sean Hansford | Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter and Damon Wilkinson Reporter 05:30, 06 Sep 2026 Updated 07:09, 06 Sep 2026 Plans for a new 'super prison' in the North West could help pave the way for the eventual closure of Strangeways , the Manchester Evening News understand This week Andy Burnham's government announced the contract for a new 1,700-place jail in Leyland, Lancs had been signed. It was part of a wider drive to 'ensure the country never again faces the nightmare of running out of prison spaces' But well-placed sources here in Manchester hope the move could help town hall bosses bolster their case for the potential closure of Strangeways. It comes three months after the MEN revealed that 'promising conversations' had been taking place with government about relocating the Speaking this week, Cheetham councillor Naeem Hassan welcomed the announcement of the new prison and said he hopes it helps usher in the end of Strangeways He said: "It's such a prime location in the city. I really want to see it moved. Prisons shouldn't be in city centres, it's not the right place. They should be in rural locations

A loved Nana of Jacob, Isaac and Isla and a dearest Mother-in-Law Service and committal at Manchester Crematorium on Monday 14th September at 2-30pm

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Top cybersecurity expert on Manchester Airports Group cyber attack risks - and what you can do about it Professor Daniel Dresner, Academic lead for Cyber Security at The University of Manchester, speaks to the Manchester Evening New Chances are if you’ve got a phone, you’ve had a scam call. Often they’re easy to spot, but sometimes they’re not as scammers lure you into a trap, usually by warning you to take urgent action to protect your assets In the digital age we live in today we’re constantly sharing information, whether that’s posting on social media or signing up for services, and this can make us vulnerable to criminals and scammers. candidates.evidence_text: Oldham 'Explosions' heard in Oldham as firefighters scrambled and over 100 homes without power Locals have reported hearing loud bangs before emergency services attended the scene Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 19:44, 05 Sep 2026 View Imag More than 100 homes were left without power after a fire at an electrical substation in Oldham. Locals reported hearing 'loud bangs' and 'explosions' as the fire broke out at the substation on Harewood Drive in Royton A video posted to social media showed bright orange flames lapping up inside it and smoke billowing out. The fire service were alerted with two fire engines attending the scene at around 5:10pm this evening (Saturday, September 5). Police were also said to be in attendance Firefighters used dry powder extinguishers in order to put out the blaze. No one was injured, Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) said Scores of locals on the neighbouring Thorp estate say their power cut out following the fire, with lights going out and dozens of house alarms sounding in the area simultaneously According to Electricity North West (ENW), at the time of writing, a total of 147 properties were still without power

Details of his death while serving his sentence at high-security HMP Wakefield prison in West Yorkshire have been confirmed by a watchdog The Prisons and Probation Ombudsman, which investigates all deaths in custody, confirmed an investigation was underway after his death on August 16. No further details have been announced Hankinson was jailed in November 2021 for 14 years. Officers were called out to London Road, near to Piccadilly Station Approach, at 6.50am this morning (September 5) Greater Manchester Police says a man in his 50s was taken to hospital after being found unresponsive, but he sadly later died. There are not currently believed to be any suspicious circumstances, but enquiries to establish the full circumstances are ongoing A large cordon was in place on London Road this morning between Aytoun Street and Store Street. Officers had erected a blue forensic tent on one part of the pavement Forensics investigators attended the scene and were seen gathering photographic evidence. candidates.evidence_text: Crime The drugs kingpin from Oldham who claimed to have met Pablo Escobar's brother in Colombia Toseef Mohammed dealt heroin and cocaine on an 'industrial scale' View 4 Images Toseef Mohammed (Image: GMP) News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 13:07, 05 Sep 2026 A drugs kingpin from Oldham claimed to have met Pablo Escobar's brother in Colombia, police have said Toseef Mohammed is behind bars after detectives smashed a heroin and cocaine ring that supplied the class A drugs on a 'commercial scale' across the North West. The 36-year-old used safe houses to store the drugs before his courier Mohammed Vakas Ashraf delivered them to customer A third member of the gang, Nicola Toft helped move and hide the money, police said. But the operation came crashing down after GMP's serious organised crime group put the gang under surveillance And when police raided a safe house owned by a vulnerable male after witnessing Mohammed pay it a visit, they discovered 60kgs of cocaine and a car which had been adapted to include a secret drugs hide. A raid on a second safe house also uncovered a large stash of cash and a deta It revealed that another 70 kilograms of cocaine and heroin had been supplied by gang between April 2025 and June 2025. In total it was established that Toft was responsible for moving and concealing nearly £460,000 in drugs money

The 36-year-old used safe houses to store the drugs before his courier Mohammed Vakas Ashraf delivered them to customer A third member of the gang, Nicola Toft helped move and hide the money, police said. But the operation came crashing down after GMP's serious organised crime group put the gang under surveillance And when police raided a safe house owned by a vulnerable male after witnessing Mohammed pay it a visit, they discovered 60kgs of cocaine and a car which had been adapted to include a secret drugs hide. A raid on a second safe house also uncovered a large stash of cash and a deta It revealed that another 70 kilograms of cocaine and heroin had been supplied by gang between April 2025 and June 2025. Carla was last seen in Piccadilly Gardens on Tuesday, August 25 Greater Manchester Police says she remains missing today (September 5). The teenager is known to have links to Manchester city centre , north Manchester and Bury She is described as being Black, around 4ft 7ins tall and with black hair, which is styled either in a bun with edges or long and loose. A photo of Carla has been shared following a number of recent appeals to find her on social media A GMP spokesperson said: "We're still trying to find Carla who has been missing since Tuesday, August 25. We're increasingly concerned for welfare. If you have any information which can help us locate her, please get in touch using the details below." Anyone who sees Carla or has information on her whereabouts is urged to come forward as soon as possible. Details can be passed on to GMP by calling 0161 856 6075, quoting log number MSO/06A2/0001292/26. In an emergency situation, dial 999

Around five Greater Manchester Police vehicles and two ambulances were seen on Church Street following the incident on Friday night (September 4) A witness reported hearing 'shouting' outside The Unicorn pub before a woman asked police to intervene. evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Christie Hospital Manchester Evening News launches £42.5m campaign to revolutionise cancer care at The Christie The Manchester Evening News is launching a joint fundraiser to expand capacity at the world-renowned hospital News Bethan Finighan Scie We want to raise £42.5m to construct a groundbreaking new scanning centre at the world-renowned hospital as demand for vital diagnostic imaging triples. The existing unit was built nearly 50 years ago to cater for around 20 patients a day Now, it supports more than 60, with demand continuing to rise as cancer diagnoses increase The Manchester Evening News is backing The Christie Charity’s £42.5m appeal. Every donation will help pave the way for the new scanning centre closer and give thousands of cancer patients access to faster and more advanced imaging DONATE TO THE SCANNING CENTRE FUNDRAISER HERE Every patient at The Christie will visit the scanning centre at some point - as part of diagnosis, during treatment or throughout ongoing follow-up care

candidates.practical_angle: Есть новый городской контекст для Greater Manchester.
candidates.lead: “I think she's a wonderful artist and I love the way she's so rude to people,” the late Tony Wilson once said of Madonna.
candidates.evidence_text: “I think she's a wonderful artist and I love the way she's so rude to people,” the late Tony Wilson once said of Madonna. And he should know The Factory Records boss had first-hand experience with the pop superstar’s brusque manner after she performed at the Haçienda in 1984 for the princely sum of £50 The bargain price gig was negotiated by television executive Malcolm Gerrie, who persuaded Madonna's record company to organise her appearance at the venue as part of a one-off, live Channel 4 broadcast of cult music show The Tube View 4 Images Madonna performing at The Hacienda, Manchester, on an episode of The Tube (Image: Channel 4/The Tube/YouTube screengrab) Free ticket-holders to the Haçienda showcase on January 27, 1984 were there to see the Factory Allstars - a band pulled together for the night by members of Durutti Column, A Certain Ratio, Quando Quango and soul singer Marcel King. So they were bemused when Madonna rocked up on Flanked by two Lycra-clad backing dancers, the then 25-year-old spun and gyrated as she sang Holiday. Her brother Christopher Ciccone - who was a backing dancer at the Haçienda gig - recounted their time in Manchester in his book, Life With My Sister

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Stockport murderer who kidnapped girl off street and sexually attacked her in horror eight-hour ordeal jailed for life Paul Sharpe held his victim hostage for eight hours before they were found by police in a hotel car park News Stephen Topping A convicted murderer who kidnapped a girl at knifepoint before sexually assaulting her has been jailed for life. Paul Sharpe held his 15-year-old victim hostage during a grim eight-hour ordeal, as he drove from one car park to another The 56-year-old put the girl in a headlock and bundled her into his car on Bradgate Road, in Altrincham , at around 7.30pm on May 18 - claiming that her father owed him money. He drove to a car park at Manchester Airport and tied up her ankles and wrists with a neck tie That night, he drove to different car parks in Greater Manchester and Cheshire, and plied the girl with alcohol while sexually assaulting her. At one point, former radio DJ Sharpe masturbated while touching the girl's feet, the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said He was finally caught by police in a hotel car park in Knutsford at around 3.40am on May 19. The girl had been reported as missing by her mother, while CCTV allowed officers to identify Sharpe's car, according to the CPS Greater Manchester Police says the girl had been studying at Sale Library on May 18 before beginning her journey home with friends at around 5:50pm. At 6:10pm, she contacted her parents to let them know she was on her way home

candidates.evidence_text: M67 Police issue major update one month after human remains discovered next to M67 Officers have made a breakthrough News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 12:27, 04 Sep 2026 View Image Police and forensics officers on the M67 after the discovery of hum Police have issued a major investigation update a month after human remains were found next to the M67 motorway. Road workers made the tragic discovery near a bridge between junctions three at Hyde and four at Hattersley on Monday. August 3 The motorway remained closed eastbound the following day as officers and forensics investigators carried out enquiries. Greater Manchester Police later confirmed that the remains were believed to belong to a man aged between 20 and 28 He was thought to have been between 5ft 5ins and 5ft 9ins tall, and of medium build. In a further update issued today (September 4), GMP says it has since identified the person's next of kin Officers are continuing to establish the circumstances of how the man ended up where he did and what caused his death. Details on when the man may have died are yet to be confirmed The discovery was made by road workers during routine maintenance on the M67, in Tameside . A Home Office post-mortem later took place as officers tried to piece together the clues of what happened to the man. Enquiries remain ongoing

candidates.evidence_text: Friday 31 July 2026 at 11:11pm More than two million voters were eligible to vote in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election as counting getsunderway. Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

Credit: Greater Manchester Police A man who killed a teenage boy on an e-bike after ramming him with his car has been jailed for 17 years Terrence King, 60, was found guilty of killing Devon Simmonds-Caines after deliberately driving his car into him on Rowrah Crescent in Middleton , Manchester King had been chasing the e-bike, which had been reportedly stolen, steering his vehicle directly at the teenager at speed without braking, on 22 July 2025 Emergency services immediately attended but despite their best efforts, Devon, aged 15, was died at the scene King was found guilty of murder at Manchester Crown Court on 17 July Following his death, Devon's family released a tribute , calling him a "bubbly person" who "only wanted the best for everyone around him"

candidates.evidence_text: New Manchester research suggests tackling the factors behind suspensions could help prevent repeated exclusions and support vulnerable pupils School suspensions are associated with a complex combination of socioeconomic disadvantage, special educational needs, peer relationships and pupils’ experiences of school, according to new research from The University of Manchester The study analysed survey responses from more than 19,000 secondary school pupils linked to administrative records across Hampshire & Isle of Wight, to examine a wide range of factors associated with whether pupils were suspended and how often suspensions occurred Researchers found pupils receiving special educational needs (SEN) support or with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) were more than twice as likely to be suspended than pupils without SEN, while those eligible for free school meals were also at increased risk The analysis also identified a number of factors associated with lower suspension risk, including pupils feeling that they belonged at school, being satisfied with their academic attainment, having positive relationships with school staff and having stronger emotion regulation sk By contrast, higher levels of peer pressure, experiences of bullying, and recent substance use were associated with an increased likelihood of suspension

A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. They will also benefit from an intensive training programme featuring cultural sector specialists and a range of prac Led by Oldham Council's Heritage, Libraries and Arts Service, the programme will be delivered in partnership with a range of organisations including Global Grooves, Northern Roots, Peshkar, Oldham Coliseum, Oldham Theatre Workshop, Oldham Sixth Form College, Mahdlo and others The initiative aims to tackle local talent drain, strengthen pathways into creative careers and ensure young people play a central role in designing and delivering Oldham's cultural activity. Earlier this year, local creatives were invited to apply for a Town of Culture micro-commission. There were 84 applications, with 13 projects chosen to receive funding Some of the successful artists and groups recently came together to mark the start of the programme. Not everyone was able to attend, but all 13 projects will play an important part in Oldham’s Town of Culture year The Oldham Panorama, a famous view of the town created in 1876, is 150 years old this year. candidates.evidence_text: A 19th century manor house in Rochdale, which has lain empty for decades, has been transformed into a café, which will formally open this weekend Nestled in the heart of Denehurst Park, the café will occupy the ground floor of Denehurst House and visitors can see it for themselves when it formally opens its doors this Saturday (5 September) More than just a café, the new venue will be managed and run by local Community Interest Company, Get Together After Serving (GTAS), and will be staffed entirely by former armed forces personnel and their families Set up by Rochdale residents, Adam Trennery, Wayne Traynor and Wayne Simms, GTAS aims to support the local veteran community in a number of ways, including through wellbeing programmes and local events and get-togethers Customers can expect café favourites like hot and cold sandwiches, cakes, breakfasts and tea and coffee, alongside generous opening hours and honest prices. The team is also hoping to team up with other local businesses to do specials on Fridays, like curry, pizza and pies. With The building has been transformed by its owners, Rochdale Borough Council, who commissioned local builders, H Bell and Sons, alongside interior design specialists, to renovate the building while honouring its period features, which include ornate coving and bay windows

candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. candidates.evidence_text: Nights you don't want to miss - Opening NightCome and join us for our first performance.Buy tickets Go behind the music and inside the story of Frankie Valli and The Four Seasons in the true-life musical phenomenon, Jersey Boys. From the streets of New Jersey to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, this is the musical that’s too good to be true. They were just four guys from Jersey, until they sang their very first note. They had a sound nobody had ever heard… and the radio just couldn’t get enough of. But while their harmonies were perfect on stage, off stage it was a very different story -- a story that has made them an international sensation all over again. The show features all their hits including “Sherry,” “Big Girls Don’t Cry,” “Walk Like A Man,” “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You,” “Beggin’,” “December 1963 (Oh What a Night)” and more. The 20th Anniversary tour boasts a stellar cast, lead by Luke Baker (Everybody’s Talking About Jamie, Sheffield/West End; Billy Elliot, Curve Leicester) as Frankie Valli, Carlo Boumouglbay (Muriel’s Wedding, Curve Leicester; Miss Saigon, international tour) as Tommy Devito, Lewis Kennedy (All male Pirates of Penzance, Wilton’s Music Hall) as Nick Massi, Toby Miles (Les Misérables, West End; School of Rock, international tour) as Bob Gaudio and Ellis Kirk (Dear Evan Hansen, West End/Asia tour) as Alternate Frankie Valli. Please note: The following performances are Access Performances - Thursday 10th September 2026 – 19:30: Audio Described Tuesday 15th September 2026 – 19:30: Captioned Buy direct from venues with ATG Tickets. Transparent booking fees, no late stage surprises. Palace Theatre Manchester The Palace Theatre of Varieties opened on Whit Monday 1891 and cost its owners the then colossal sum of £40,500. In the late 1970’s the Palace Theatre underwent a major refurbishment and re-opened in 1981 with Andrew Lloyd Webber’s Jesus Christ Superstar and has since then retained its position as the premier provincial touring venue

It blends village charm with urban convenience and a vibrant community atmosphere. It boasts gorgeous historic buildings alongside a whole network of trendy, independent hospitality and retail businesses. And it Hidden beneath the surface of all this are stories. Lots and lots of stories. From screen-worthy romances to notorious murderers via whole potato-swallowers and eccentric aldermen, Didsbury has the lot. candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Central Library , Manchester Until 20 December 2026 Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit Manchester has always been a city with stories to tell. This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.evidence_text: 420 works fill HOME’s main gallery, chosen from more than 1,500 entries submitted from across all 10 Greater Manchester boroughs HOME Manchester , Manchester Until 6 September 2026 Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit Four editions in, the Manchester Open has become both a biennial survey of the region’s creative output and a quiet argument about who gets seen in the art world. The format is open submission, anonymous selection, a panel drawn from practicing artists, community members and art This summer, 420 works fill HOME’s main gallery, chosen from more than 1,500 entries submitted from across all 10 Greater Manchester boroughs. The youngest artist is four; the oldest nearly 80. The range of media – painting, ceramics, photography, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, Clarissa Corfe, HOME’s Creative Producer for Visual Art, describes the works as revealing “something of the relationship we have with ourselves, family, community and the natural world, demonstrated through layers of nuance, imagination, wit and resonance.” Go with a friend and y The exhibition itself doesn’t try to resolve the question of what’s best – but the awards do. Three artist development packages are awarded in partnership with Castlefield Gallery, alongside a HOME Award offering a solo show in the Granada Foundation Galleries. The Kate Vokes Peo

Whilst nearby Fallowfield and Withington cater to a grungier student crowd, Didsbury services a mixed bag of young professionals, families, retirees and, of course, their fashionable dogs- almost If you’re after cafes, Didsbury has them in droves. Our favourite is La Chouquette , a Parisian-style patisserie at the bottom of the highstreet. He’s a good Richarlison has spent the week training separately from the first team, but De Zerbi denied cutting the Brazilian adrift, insisting: “He decided everything. candidates.evidence_text: 8 ноября 2026 года в Indigo at The O2 состоится концерт GORAN BREGOVIC в Лондоне Имя Горана Бреговича давно стало символом целого музыкального мира. Его путь начался в многонациональном Сараеве, где восточные мотивы естественно переплетались с западными традициями, а каждая улица имела свой ритм. Именно эта атмосфера сформировала композитора, впоследствии воз Впоследствии музыка Бреговича вышла за рамки концертных площадок. Сотрудничество с режиссером Emir Kusturica подарило мировому кинематографу саундтреки, ставшие неотъемлемой частью фильмов Time of the Gypsies, Arizona Dream и Underground. В этих мелодиях живут Балканы — с их своб Популярность Бреговича родилась не только благодаря знаменитым композициям “Kalashnikov”, “Ederlezi”, “In the Death Car” или “Bella Ciao”. Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. Вместе с легендарным “Wedding and Funera Окунитесь в этот балканский водоворот прямо в самом сердце Лондона! Город, который веками принимал выступления и разные культуры со всех континентов, на один вечер станет местом встречи британской сдержанности и безудержной балканской страсти. И, возможно, именно эта неожиданная Чтобы попасть на концерт GORAN BREGOVIC в Лондоне, покупайте билеты на нашем сайте и в кассах города. Еще больше концертов в афише Лондона ищите у нас на сайте

candidates.evidence_text: As AI adoption gathers pace, organisations are under growing pressure to invest and demonstrate where the technology can deliver meaningful business value This lunchtime session brings together senior technology leaders with first-hand experience of putting AI into practice. Speakers will share what they have learned from implementing AI, including the technical, operational and organisational challenges encountered along the way There will also be an opportunity to put your questions to the panel and connect with fellow technology leaders over lunch 📅 Date: Thursday 1st October 2026 🕒 Time: 12pm-2pm 📍 Location: No.1 Circle Square 💷 Price: Manchester Digital members - Free (4 x tickets per company) Non members - £30 Spaces are limited - secure your place to gain insight from these senior leaders and connect with peers
